nodes.name: HighScope Perry Preschool study
nodes.description: A preschool experiment involving 123 children in Ypsilanti, Michigan during the 1960s. Subsequent reassignment compromised the initial randomization, requiring adjustment in later analyses.

nodes.name: The $4-9 ROI figure comes from long-term studies (Perry Preschool, Abecedarian). Short-term budget cycles rarely capture these multi-decade returns, making them politically undervalued.
Perry Preschool initial program cost: 17,759 USD per child (2006 prices)
nodes.description: An undiscounted program resource cost per child, including operating expenses and classroom facilities. It is not annual expenditure or the financing-adjusted denominator for every economic scenario.

nodes.name: The rate of return to the HighScope Perry Preschool Program
nodes.description: An economic analysis of the HighScope Perry Preschool experiment, published in 2010. It estimates returns while accounting for compromised randomization and uncertainty in projected outcomes.

nodes.name: Perry Preschool: costs, observed outcomes and modeled returns
nodes.description: Study evidence from a preschool intervention in Ypsilanti, Michigan. Costs, descriptive outcomes and modeled economic returns retain their distinct assumptions and source context.
